newsitem.title: CHINA: INTERVIEW- CCT seeks closer China ties.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW- CCT seeks closer China ties.

text.p: Loss-making CCT Telecom Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it was aiming to turn the company around this year and plans to shore up its future earnings through expansion into China.
"Our ambition is to turn this loss-making company around this year," managing director Bankee Kwan told Reuters in an interview.
CCT Telecom, the largest maker of facsimile machines in Hong Kong, posted a net loss of HK$121.6 million in 1996.
The company, which also makes telephones and answering machines, was hit by the continued slowdown in worldwide electronic consumer markets in 1996.
During a drastic eight-month reorganisation, Kwan said losses were written off, management was changed, and relations with customers improved.
"The chairman found the old management team, which was on contract basis, were non-performing and scrapped the board totally," he said.
Kwan, who joined the company in the autumn last year, said he felt the company was now in good shape and ready to contemplate new ventures.
"Now CCT has new missions," Kwan said.
About 60-70 percent of CCT's sales were from Europe and the United States, and China was still an unexplored market to the company, Kwan said.
The company intends to become the largest telecom products maker in Hong Kong. It also plans to diversify into China's telecommunications industry.
"We hope future China revenues will account for about 20-30 percent of our income," Kwan said.

CCT is now exploring China's fledgling telecommunications industry and is in preliminary talks with Chinese partners, including Chinese Internet Corp (CIC) which is controlled by China's state Xinhua news agency.
"We have talks with CIC relating to a number of projects," Kwan said, but added that no announcements should be expected soon.
CCT has already established ties with Xinhua following Thursday's shareholder approval to place 200 million new shares, or 12.51 percent of the company, to Xinhua unit Golden Tripod (Holdings) Ltd.

"We hope Xinhua will introduce good telecommunication projects to us and since it is our shareholder we hope they can provide us with assistance in establishing good relationships in China," Kwan said.
He said CCT would not exclude any opportunity to work with any government department, including the influential Ministry of Posts & Telecommunications (MPT).
"There are chances to co-operate with every department in China," Kwan said.
CCT Telecom is no stranger to China's MPT.

In 1994, China Treasure Telecom Holdings Ltd, which later changed its name to CCT Telecom, formed a joint venture with MPT in Shandong, China to make moblie telecommunications equipment and to develop a radio telephone paging system.
But Kwan said the joint venture was later closed down due to market problems.
China's telecommunications market is still heavily regulated and CCT needs to jump through a lot of hoops and get a number of approvals before any investment is possible, Kwan said.
CCT plans to invite other strategic shareholders and long-term investors into the company, but he mentioned no names.
CCT has HK$270 million cash on hand which will be used as working capital to invest in China.
